focus: Every reader gap, ranked by whether a fix would move a published number

keyQuestions: (c) Which runtimes still have a reader or attribution gap the arm cannot see — codex unmeasured under Q075, devin and dsh one unknown row each, opencode all unknown — and what file line proves each gap?
answeredQuestions: (c) Which runtimes still have a reader or attribution gap the arm cannot see — codex unmeasured under Q075, devin and dsh one unknown row each, opencode all unknown — and what file line proves each gap?
ruledOut: Treating Codex as a sixth measured runtime
Reading devin and dsh offerUnknown as a lost offer

label: Codex has no rows because the runner refuses the whole arm when the project hook is unapproved: it writes codex-hooks-unapproved with measurable false and the /hooks repair text before any turn runs, and Q075 is the operator leaving Codex out.

Approving the Codex hook does not by itself produce a delivery boolean: the reader returns false only when unapproved and otherwise unknown unless the session records or injected block carry the brief, so an approved Codex arm can print the same unknown as OpenCode.

OpenCode unknown is documented as design: the plugin adds the brief in memory and the store keeps no copy, and the suite pins unknown even for a session whose records hold the brief at command-offer.vitest.ts:259-265, so a receipt alone would not move the number.

The devin and dsh single offerUnknown row is a run-line format gap: offerFieldAbsent is true when the line carries no offer field and a scored owned row is then counted apart rather than as a non-offer.

Reader gaps rank OpenCode then Codex then Devin/DSH by published-number impact: OpenCode carries 80 of 80 lines unknown, Devin and DSH lose one row each which cannot move a rate over 28, and Codex has 0 rows so its fix unlocks a runtime rather than correcting a number.
